module purpose: The supplied neorv32_sys RTL implements two service blocks: neorv32_sys_reset sequences and synchronizes reset outputs from external, watchdog and debug reset inputs, and neorv32_sys_clock latches an enable request, counts enabled cycles, and generates divided one-cycle clock-enable pulses on clk_en_o.

use-case flows.value: external reset clears the reset sequencers and forces rstn_ext_o, rstn_sys_o, xrstn_wdt_o and xrstn_ocd_o low
external reset release is delayed by shifting '1' through sreg_ext and driving rstn_ext_o from and_reduce_f(sreg_ext)
system reset release is delayed while rstn_wdt_i and rstn_dbg_i stay high, otherwise sreg_sys is cleared, and rstn_sys_o follows and_reduce_f(sreg_sys)
watchdog and debug reset inputs are synchronized into xrstn_wdt_o and xrstn_ocd_o
rstn_i clears the clock-enable generator state en, cnt and cnt2
the OR-reduced enable request is latched into en to start or stop counting
enabled-cycle counting and previous-count capture generate one-cycle divided clock-enable pulses on clk_en_o

conceptual assets.concept: External reset-release sequence state and output
conceptual assets.reasoning: The reset flow forces `sreg_ext <= (others => '0')` and `rstn_ext_o <= '0'` when `rstn_ext_i = '0'` (lines 45-46). After reset is inactive, `sreg_ext <= sreg_ext(sreg_ext'left-1 downto 0) & '1'` (line 51) and `rstn_ext_o <= and_reduce_f(sreg_ext)` (line 52). Integrity matters because the reset value delivered to other logic must follow this staged release sequence; availability is also established because with `rstn_ext_i = '1'` and rising clocks, the sequence reaches the all-'1' state and `rstn_ext_o` can deassert.

conceptual assets.concept: System reset-release sequence qualified by watchdog and debug reset inputs
conceptual assets.reasoning: The reset flow forces `sreg_sys` and `rstn_sys_o` low on external reset (lines 47-48). On each rising edge, `sreg_sys` is cleared again if `(rstn_wdt_i = '0') or (rstn_dbg_i = '0')` (lines 54-55), else it shifts in '1' (line 57); `rstn_sys_o <= and_reduce_f(sreg_sys)` (line 59). Integrity matters because system-reset release must reflect both the staged sequence and these qualifying conditions; availability is established when external reset is inactive, both qualifiers stay high, and clocks continue.

conceptual assets.concept: Synchronized watchdog-reset value delivered to other logic
conceptual assets.reasoning: The synchronizer forces `xrstn_wdt_o <= '0'` on external reset (line 69) and otherwise captures `xrstn_wdt_o <= rstn_wdt_i` on each rising edge (line 72). Under the module-boundary integrity assumption, consumers depend on receiving exactly this registered reset value; availability is established whenever external reset is inactive and a clock edge occurs.

conceptual assets.concept: Synchronized debug-reset value delivered to other logic
conceptual assets.reasoning: The synchronizer forces `xrstn_ocd_o <= '0'` on external reset (line 70) and otherwise captures `xrstn_ocd_o <= rstn_dbg_i` on each rising edge (line 73). Under the module-boundary integrity assumption, consumers depend on receiving exactly this registered reset value; availability is established whenever external reset is inactive and a clock edge occurs.

`en <= or_reduce_f(enable_i)` stores a one-bit decision on the clock edge (line 129), and the next statements use `if (en = '1')` to choose between incrementing `cnt` and clearing it (lines 130-133). Integrity matters because counting and the later clock-enable pulse schedule depend on this stored decision; availability is established because the decision is produced on each rising edge from the current `enable_i` reduction. `enable_i` is a clock-enable input and is not reported as a structural reference under the exclusion rule.

conceptual assets.concept: Divider phase state and generated clock-enable pulse vector
conceptual assets.reasoning: While the latched enable remains high, `cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(cnt) + 1)` updates the phase state (line 131) and `cnt2 <= cnt` captures the previous phase (line 135); when disabled, `cnt <= (others => '0')` resets the phase (line 133). Each output pulse is then defined by `clk_en_o(...) <= cnt(bit) and (not cnt2(bit))` at lines 140-147. Integrity matters because both the pulse positions and which divided enable fires depend on these two stored phase values. Availability is also established: with continued enabled clocks, the phase advances and the output expressions recurrently assert pulses. The FLOW GRAPH leaves `clk_en_o` unreached, but the element records at lines 140-147 explicitly give its GATED_BY dependence on `cnt` and `cnt2`.
